specific_issues: The "Highest-Severity Events" table lists severity-9.0/9.2 "Conflict" and "Political Violence Targeting Civilians" entries with actor pairs like "MONROVIA <-> THE US" and "POLICE OFFICER <-> FIRE DEPARTMENT" that the report itself later admits (in the Coverage note) are misclassified noise (e.g., a Culver City wildfire story). Presenting these as top "Highest-Severity Events" in a ranked table before explaining the caveat is misleading to a reader skimming the table, and assigning them numeric severities of 9.0-9.2 alongside real events (cocaine bust charges) conflates unrelated signal quality.

Dataset summary shows only 21 "conflict" events, 2 "political_violence_targeting_civilians" events, and 2 ACLED entries total, yet the Political & Security Landscape table reports "Total Events 27, Critical(≥7) 16, High(5-6.9) 10, Fatalities 0" — the relationship between these figures and the stated dataset totals (21 conflict + 2 pol-violence = 23, not 27) is not reconciled or explained, raising a possible arithmetic/scope inconsistency.

The report states "AidData records over 150 grant-based commitments from Chinese government institutions and the Ministry of Commerce" and later "Unspecified Chinese Government Institution (118 records) and China's Ministry of Commerce (36 records)" — 118+36=154, consistent internally, but the dataset summary shows AidData total = 213 records overall (which would include non-Chinese-government-institution entries), so the report's claim that Chinese state financiers "account for well over half of all recorded investment activity" (228 investment records total per dataset summary) is plausible but not clearly cross-verified against the 228 investment-category figure — the report never explicitly ties its financier counts back to the 228 total investment records, leaving the "well over half" claim unverified from the text alone.

The Risk Scorecard shows "Political Stability 0.2" (very low) directly juxtaposed with a Security sub-score of 5.2 and extensive narrative about a "governance crisis" — the sharp divergence is explained in a footnote but the placement (raw score table before explanation) could confuse readers about why political risk is scored so low despite the scandal narrative dominating the brief.

Note 8 attributes "Analytical narrative sections generated by Anthropic Claude" — an unusual level of internal-process disclosure for a client-facing institutional brief; combined with the AI-generated caveat embedded in the footer, this undercuts the polished "JPMorgan-circulated" positioning the brief otherwise aims for.

The report cites "emansion.gov.lr" repeatedly as a source but this is never listed in the numbered Notes/citation list (Notes 1-8 cover ACLED, AidData, DFC, GDELT, IMF, WorldBank, WorldBankPPI, and Claude-narrative — emansion.gov.lr, liberianobserver.com, and general "open-web reporting" are cited in-text but have no corresponding formal citation entries), a citation-completeness gap.

"Overall risk score: 2.9/10 (Low)" is presented with high precision/confidence despite the report's own acknowledgment of GDELT noise, unverified political-violence entries, and multi-year gaps in financing data — the false precision (one decimal place) is not caveated at the point of presentation.

Filter or flag known-noise events (e.g., misclassified foreign wildfire stories) before they enter any "Highest-Severity Events" ranked table; only surface the caveat inline in that table (e.g., "[Note: likely misclassified, see Coverage Note]") rather than only in a separate section that a reader may not reach.

Add an explicit reconciliation line whenever headline counts (e.g., Total Events 27) are used, showing how they derive from the underlying category counts (conflict + political_violence + protest events) so readers/auditors can verify the arithmetic against the dataset summary.

When citing "well over half of all recorded investment activity" for Chinese financiers, explicitly state the denominator (e.g., "154 of 228 investment records, or 68%") rather than leaving the reader to infer the percentage.

Move the sub-score methodology footnote (explaining why Political Stability can be near-zero despite an active scandal) to immediately precede or accompany the Risk Scorecard table, not after it, to avoid an apparent contradiction on first read.

Either remove the "generated by Anthropic Claude" disclosure from the client-facing notes or relocate it to an internal methodology appendix separate from the main citation list, to preserve institutional tone consistency.

Add emansion.gov.lr, liberianobserver.com, and "open-web reporting" (specify actual outlet names where possible, e.g., AOL/AP wire) as proper numbered Chicago-style source notes so every in-text citation maps to a formal reference.

Round or qualify the overall risk score (e.g., "approximately 3/10, Low, with elevated uncertainty given data-quality caveats noted above") rather than presenting a one-decimal figure that implies false precision.
